plot: At sunset on the beach Grandma loses the golden key to her house; Dog digs ten empty holes, Bird proudly brings back a banana and a red ball, and Max walks in circles until he is dizzy, until Grandma remembers the key always smells of cookies, so Max asks Dog to use his nose instead of his paws, and Dog sniffs the key out under Grandma's towel.

beats.say: Oh dear! Oh dear, oh dear! My golden key is gone!
It is the end of a lovely day at the beach. The sun is sinking into the sea.
Grandma, what key? The key to your house?
Yes. It is little and gold, with a round top. Without it, we can't get inside.
Don't worry, Grandma. We will find it before the sun goes down!
Finding things in sand? That is my favorite job! Dig, dig, dig!
Dog digs one hole. Then two holes. Then ten holes. Sand flies everywhere.
Dog! You are making a beach full of holes!
Holes are great. But there is no key in any of them.
Thank you for trying, dear. But please, no more holes. I might fall in one!
I will help! I am the best at finding shiny things. Be right back!
Bird flies away, and quickly comes back with something yellow.
Look! It is yellow. That is almost gold. Is this the key?
That is a banana, dear. A very nice banana. But it can't open a door.
Wait, wait! I will find a better one!
This time, Bird comes back with a round, red ball.
My ball! My lost ball from last summer! Bird, you are the best finder ever!
It is a great find. But it is still not Grandma's key.
Okay. I will be a detective. I will walk in a big circle and look very carefully.
Max walks in a circle. Then a smaller circle. Then a tiny circle, and he gets dizzy.
Whoa. The beach is spinning. Or maybe it's me.
Max, you look like a sleepy spinning top!
Grandma, let's think. Where was the key this morning?
It was in my pocket. And before that, it was hanging by my cookie jar.
That key always smells a little bit like cookies.
Cookies! Grandma, that's it! Dog can smell cookies from very far away!
That's true. I can smell a cookie from the other side of town.
Then stop using your paws, Dog, and use your nose! Find the cookie smell!
Dog puts his nose down on the sand. Sniff. Sniff, sniff. Sniff, sniff, sniff.
Seaweed. Shells. Sunscreen. Fish. Oh! Cookies! I smell cookies!
Dog follows his nose across the sand, past all his holes, right to Grandma's beach towel.
There, under the corner of the towel, is a little golden key with a round top.
My key! It must have slipped out when I shook the sand off my towel.
I found it! Me! With my nose! Not with my paws!
Dog found it with his nose? I did not know noses could find things!
Dog, your nose is a super nose.
Dog carries the key to Grandma, very gently, in his mouth.
Thank you, Dog. And thank you, Max, for thinking about what Dog is best at.
Everybody is good at something. Bird finds shiny things, and Dog finds smells.
And I found a banana and a ball! That is two things!
You did, dear. And we will share the banana on the way home.
Dog fills all his holes back in, so nobody trips. Max helps him pat the sand flat.
Goodbye, holes. You were very nice holes.
Don't be sad, Dog. Your nose was the real hero today.
Then they walk home together, as the last light turns the sea pink and gold.
Grandma, can we put your key on a string, so it never runs away again?
What a good idea, Max. A string with a little bell on it.
Then let's make Grandma's key the jingliest key in the whole town!
